heading.en: From ideas to a good essay

hook.en: Two students can have the same ideas and get very different marks. The difference is structure, paragraphing and language.

objectives.en: Structure a composition with an introduction, body paragraphs and a conclusion
Choose vivid, precise language and vary sentences

narration.en: Two students can have the same ideas and get very different marks. The difference is structure, paragraphing and language.

body.en: Every composition needs a beginning that catches interest and sets the direction, a body of well-developed paragraphs, and an ending that rounds off the piece (a resolution, a final image, or a conclusion that follows from the argument). Each paragraph deals with one main idea, usually announced in a topic sentence and supported with details, examples or events. Paragraphs are linked by transitions: however, as a result, a moment later, on the other hand, above all.

label.en: Words per minute to finish in 35 minutes

body.en: Use precise, vivid words rather than vague ones (strolled, limped or marched instead of went). Show rather than tell in narratives: describe the shaking hands instead of saying "I was nervous". Vary sentence length and openings; a short sentence after long ones gives punch. Keep tenses consistent, avoid slang and clichés, and use figures of speech only where they add something. Leave time to proofread for spelling, agreement and punctuation errors.

prompt.en: Put these parts of a short narrative composition in a sensible order.

narration.en: Put these parts of a short narrative composition in a sensible order.

steps.en: The night before the exam, the power went off across the hostel.
At first we laughed and lit a single candle, sure it would come back soon.
By midnight the candle was a stub, and panic crept into the room.
Then Meena remembered the old emergency lamp in the warden's office.
We studied in a circle round its yellow light until dawn.
I still keep a candle on my desk to remind me how we turned a crisis into teamwork.

explanation.en: Situation, first reaction, rising tension, turning point, resolution, reflection: a clear narrative arc.

problem.en: Improve this sentence: "It was a very nice day and I went to the park and it was very nice and there were lots of people."

steps.en: Replace vague words: "very nice" → bright and breezy; "lots of people" → families, joggers and kite-flyers.
Remove repetition and split the run-on sentence.
"It was a bright, breezy Sunday. The park was full of families, joggers and kite-flyers, and the air smelt of roasted corn."

answer.en: Two clear sentences with precise, vivid detail instead of one vague run-on.
